questionText:
Which of the following statement is not true about mahajanapadas of the
sixth-century BCE:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Assumed both statements were correct.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies that both statements contain factual errors.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
The sixth century BCE is regarded as a major turning point in early Indian history, marked by the emergence of sixteen major territorial states called mahajanapadas. Buddhist and Jaina texts list sixteen states (such as Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, and Avanti). While most were monarchies ruled by rajas, some were oligarchies known as ganas or sanghas (like the Vajji sangha). Each had a fortified capital city, and rulers maintained standing armies and administrative bureaucracies. Stating that texts mention twenty states is factually incorrect.
Hence, option (B) is correct.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Letters may be faintly engraved, inscriptions may be damaged, reconstruction of words is uncertain, and elite inscriptions omit routine daily life events of ordinary peasants
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for The Limitations of Inscriptional Evidence.

options.text: Inscriptions can only be translated using automated computer software
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Inscriptions were made of radioactive stone materials dangerous to inspect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For The Limitations of Inscriptional Evidence (Political and Economic Systems in Early States (Kings, Farmers and Towns)):
1. Epigraphy has limitations: letters are faint, stone surfaces weather away, meanings of technical terms remain uncertain, and elite biases ignore common people's lives.
Hence Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 49.13] The vast majority of the rock edicts and pillar inscriptions of Mauryan Emperor Ashoka were written in which script and language?

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Ashokan Inscriptions and Dhamma.

options.text: Greek script and Aramaic language exclusively
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Political and Economic Systems in Early States (Kings, Farmers and Towns) (Ashokan Inscriptions and Dhamma):
Brahmi script and Prakrit language

Detailed Context:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Kings, Farmers and Towns - Ashokan Inscriptions and Dhamma):
Most Ashokan inscriptions were in the Prakrit language using the Brahmi script. In the northwest (modern Afghanistan/Pakistan), inscriptions were also carved in Aramaic and Greek, and in Kharosthi script.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Names) List-II (Associations)
(A) Piyadassi
(I) Script
(B) Kalinga
(II) Reporter
(C) Kharosthi
(III) Asoka
(D) Pativedaka (IV) Coastal Orissa
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Detailed Solution:
Epigraphic terms: 'Piyadassi' (pleasant to behold) was the standard honorific title used by Emperor Asoka in his rock and pillar edicts (A-(III)). Kalinga was the ancient name for coastal Odisha conquered in Ashoka's eighth regnal year (B-(IV)). Kharosthi was the right-to-left script used for Ashokan edicts in the northwest (C-(I)). In Major Rock Edict VI, Ashoka commanded the 'pativedakas' (special reporters) to report public affairs to him at all times and places (D-(II)). Match: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.
